title: [docs-infra] Retire the docs service worker
body:
mui.com renders and then immediately reloads itself on the first visit after a deploy. The service worker causes it, and the reload no longer does anything useful.

`sw.js` stopped caching in #37607, when workbox was removed and the file became a no-op kill switch. That commit only touched `sw.js`, so the registration, the `forcePageReload`/`lazyReload` machinery and the `// uuid: <date>` stamped into the file on every build all stayed behind. The uuid guarantees the browser finds a new worker after every deploy, which activates, which fires `lazyReload()`.

The reload did have a real job between #14122 and #37607: the worker served `/` and `*.js` with `staleWhileRevalidate`, so a post-deploy reload is what moved you onto fresh content. There is no cache any more, and the worker has no `fetch` handler, so it is not in the request path and can neither cause nor cure staleness.

`/sw.js` keeps being served, now as a worker that unregisters itself and clears the caches workbox left behind. Deleting the file is not a reliable way to clear an existing registration across browsers, whereas a self-unregistering worker picked up by the browser's soft update check is. Once it has had time to reach returning visitors the file can go too.

The later commits move the llms docs cleanup into `buildLlmsDocs`. `docs:llms:build` used to `rimraf` the whole output folder, so that folder could not hold anything but generated files. The script now globs the previous run's output inside that folder and removes it, leaving any other file alone. That part is independent of the service worker here, where `sw.js` sits at the public root; it is what mui/mui-x#23674 needs in order to serve its worker from `docs/public/x`. Happy to split it out if you would rather review it separately.

`docs:build-sw` in the root package.json still pointed at the script this PR deletes, so it goes too.

Deployment skew is already handled by Next: a stale chunk 404s, `markAssetError` fires, and the router hard-navigates to the target URL. Skew protection is not involved either, since it needs the Netlify Next.js runtime and the docs are a static export.

MUI X registers through the same `DocsApp`, so this also stops the reload on mui.com/x. mui/mui-x#23674 retires the worker it serves at `/x/sw.js`, and should land after this one.
